liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Sucking and squishing audio during transition to Franklin's Tower; Enormous, shuddering opening starts the set off hot [18][27]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drumming ranks among the best the band has done [24]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Drummers stay on stage for improvisation during Space section [24]
- Jerry Garcia wails on solos during the song [19]
- Jerry turns up solos, making the crowd scream [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-11-29.132457.wise.aud.flac24** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 178 min [1]
- **gd80-11-29.wise.sacks.2409.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 179 min; rated 4.79/5 by 58 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has bright sound, though slightly clunky; Listener considers this the best audience recording they have heard; Taper found a sweet spot, making it decent [18][19][26]
- **gd1980-11-29.nak700.wagner.miller.90104.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 182 min; rated 4.5/5 by 14 [8]
- **gd1980-11-29.beyer160.wise.gmb.89938.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 4.89/5 by 9 [12]. Said about its sound: Slight digital noise present at the end of Stella Blue [12]
- **gd1980-11-29.175074.set2.sbd.miller.vocal-phase-repair.flac2496**: soundboard; 11 songs; 103 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [15]

## Around the show

- Audience member shouts 'Down for the harvest?' at start [21]
- Crowd is raucous and appreciative, similar to Radio City audiences [23]
- It was snowing on the beach in Florida [26]
- Show smokes more than previous months despite no acoustic set [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-11-29.132457.wise.aud.flac24**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Cassette Audience Master recorded By Jim Wise (patched out of MadRiverRich); Beyer dynamic M160 Double Ribbon Hypercardiod microphones mounted on a stand-Sony… [1]. Also: Setlist includes encores Casey Jones and Mexicali Blues [1]
- **gd80-11-29.wise.sacks.2409.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Beyer M-160's [3]
- **gd1980-11-29.nak700.wagner.miller.90104.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony D5M/TDK SA-X90/Dolby DB) D [8]. Also: FOB Beyer M-160 to cassette, then Alesis Masterlink to CD; Bob Wagner lent masters; Jim Wise recorded patch source [8]
- **gd1980-11-29.beyer160.wise.gmb.89938.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Beyer M-160's > Sony TC-D5 > CDR > DAT [12]. Also: Crossfades applied for tape flips and between first set tunes [12]
- **gd1980-11-29.175074.set2.sbd.miller.vocal-phase-repair.flac2496**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 8, 2025; source: SBD > Multi-Gen Cassette (Maxell XLII 90) [15]. Also: Vocal phase repair of soundboard tape from Sean Kutzko; Jim Wise provided patch source; Joe B. Jones set pitch [15]

claims.text: Audience recording has bright sound, though slightly clunky
Sucking and squishing audio during transition to Franklin's Tower
Listener considers this the best audience recording they have heard
Jerry Garcia wails on solos during the song
Audience member shouts 'Down for the harvest?' at start
Crowd is raucous and appreciative, similar to Radio City audiences
Show smokes more than previous months despite no acoustic set
Drummers stay on stage for improvisation during Space section
Drumming ranks among the best the band has done
It was snowing on the beach in Florida
Taper found a sweet spot, making it decent
Enormous, shuddering opening starts the set off hot
Jerry turns up solos, making the crowd scream
Setlist includes encores Casey Jones and Mexicali Blues
FOB Beyer M-160 to cassette, then Alesis Masterlink to CD
Bob Wagner lent masters; Jim Wise recorded patch source
Crossfades applied for tape flips and between first set tunes
Slight digital noise present at the end of Stella Blue
Vocal phase repair of soundboard tape from Sean Kutzko
Jim Wise provided patch source; Joe B. Jones set pitch
